REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 26, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
APRIL 26, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by City Clerk Vida Barone.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Boy Scout Troop 888.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Ryan Chiang, Isaiah David Tang, and Charles Taylor (Achieving the rank of
  Eagle Scout)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  David Pylman spoke regarding the City Council meeting procedures and
  thanked staff for their customer service.

  Yanet Lindner expressed concern with the City’s parking permit program. She
  submitted a document for the record.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding various architectural features within City
  facilities.

  Luke Sutanto expressed concern with the City’s parking permit program.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
  by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  April 12, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of April 12, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Register of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 26,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  4/26/2018  $4,183,802.15  (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s report for the period ending March 31,

  Treasurer's reports for the  period  ending  March  31,  2018.
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 26, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of City of Cerritos Facebook page comments policy
  and posting protocol (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to not move
  forward with implementation of a City of Cerritos Official Facebook page at this
  time (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of two-year extension to the contract between the
  City of Cerritos and the City of Long Beach Animal care services for the
  provision of animal control and sheltering services for the period of July 1,
  2018 through June 30, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Approve a two-year contract extension with the City of Long Beach Animal
  care services for the provision of animal control and sheltering services for
  the period of July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2020 in the sum of $347,735
  for Fiscal Year 2018, and;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign all necessary documentation on behalf
  of the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 26, 2018

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Solanki, to approve
  a modification to the 2018 City Council/Successor Agency meeting schedule by
  changing the City Council/Successor Agency meeting date from Monday, June

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido

  ABSENT:  None

9D.  Award of Bid No. 1335-18, purchase of new motor control system for the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Thomas Hamilton, CCPA Technical Administrator.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to award Bid No.
  1335-18 to Skjonberk Controls for the purchase and installation of a new
  motor control system in the amount of $84,985.85 and reject all other bids
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Award of Bid No. 1336-18, contract for Carmenita Road rehabilitation, Project
  No. 18301 (COUNCIL).

  Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works, requested that the item to be
  moved to a subsequent meeting.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.
